# JustGivenUp! Browser Extension (Chrome / Firefox, MV3)

The in-browser layer of the guardian:

* **Static blocking rules** (`rules.json`, ~12k adult domains) — generated by
  `scripts/build_blocklist.py`. Main-frame hits are redirected to a
  motivational interstitial (`blocked.html`) which also logs the attempt to
  the local dashboard; sub-resources are blocked outright.
* **Safe-search hardening** — forces `safe=active` on Google, `adlt=strict`
  on Bing and strict SafeSearch on DuckDuckGo.
* **Heartbeat** (`background.js`) — proves to the daemon every minute that
  the extension is alive. If browsers are open for 15+ minutes with no
  heartbeat **while a lock is active**, the daemon treats it as removal
  and extends the lock by 90 days.
* **Custom domains** — domains you add in the dashboard arrive as dynamic
  rules without reloading the extension.
* **Read-only UI** — the popup and options pages show status only. There is
  no "disable" button here on purpose: settings live in the dashboard, and
  while the time-lock runs the extension cannot be talked into weakening
  itself.

## Install — Chrome / Edge / Brave / Vivaldi / Chromium

1. Open `chrome://extensions`
2. Enable **Developer mode** (top right)
3. Click **Load unpacked** and select this `extension/` directory
4. Pin the shield icon — you will see the lock countdown

> The Debian package additionally ships an **enterprise policy**
> (`URLBlocklist`) that blocks the same domains at the browser level and
> cannot be toggled off by the user at all — the extension then only adds
> the interstitial, countdown and dashboard integration.

## Install — Firefox / Firefox ESR / LibreWolf

1. Open `about:addons`
2. Gear icon → **Install Add-on From File…**
3. Select `extension/justgivenup.xpi` (built by `scripts/pack_extension.sh`)
   — or, for development: `about:debugging#/runtime/this-firefox` →
   **Load Temporary Add-on…** → pick `manifest.json`

The `.deb` package also installs a Firefox enterprise policy that blocks
the same domains system-wide (see `packaging/deb/DEBIAN/postinst`).

## Notes

* The extension expects the local daemon at `http://127.0.0.1:8081`.
  Without the daemon everything still blocks (static rules), you just do
  not get the countdown/heartbeat integration.
* `manifest.firefox.json` is the Firefox variant; the packaging script
  swaps it in when building `justgivenup.xpi`.
* Host permission for `<all_urls>` is required by `declarativeNetRequest`
  redirects; traffic is never read or sent anywhere — all requests to the
  daemon stay on `127.0.0.1`.
